newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - April 21.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - April 21.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the South African press on Monday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
BUSINESS DAY

- The Land Bank would expand rather than change its focus in order to serve black farmers and their white colleagues, its new executive director Helena Dolny said on Sunday. The appointment of Dolny, Communist Party leader Joe Slovo's widow, to the post has been criticised by white farmers.

- Wide-ranging changes to the funding and governance of higher education institutions, but which stop short of some drastic changes demanded by students organisations, have been published in draft form by the education ministry.

- Dolphin Group president Ketan Somaia arrived in South Africa last week to launch a public relations campaign designed to convince the public of his credibility -- just days after refusing to appear before a Kenyan public accounts committee hearing on alleged tender fraud.

- Randgold and Exploration Co Ltd was likely to place control of its Blyvooruitzicht Gold Mining Co Ltd and Buffelsfontein Gold Mines Ltd gold mines into Durban Roodepoort Deep Ltd in a move which furthered its cost-cutting restructuring drive, sources close to the gold mining house said at the weekend.

- The National Party (NP) has called for the suspension of several top Independent Broadcasting Authority councillors and senior managers following accusations of financial mismanagement in a preliminary Auditor General's report.

- Western Cape tow truck drivers will be unable to tap into the police service's "walkie talkie" network to identify accident scenes from September, when the province's new radio network comes into operation.
BUSINESS REPORT

- The Congress of South African Trade Unions' (Cosatu's) national executive has scaled down its 24-hour national strike over planned employment legislation scheduled for May 12 to marches and rallies.

- Spiralling cheque fraud in government departments will cost taxpayers well over 120 million rand this year, Willy Goldswain, the marketing and sales consultant of Synchron Security Products, a fraud investigator, said at the weekend.

- Neill Bernstein, a 33-year-old Cape Town businessman and property developer, said at the weekend he was acquiring an 84 percent stake in IB Joffe Ltd, the manufacturer and distributor of camping and outdoor equipment, for about 8,5 million rand.

- The 67 offices of the South African Revenue Services throughout the country have embarked on a series of swoops on businesses to round up tax evaders and to establish a culture of co-operation with the tax authorities.

- The decision by the European Commission to force Anglo American Corp to reduce its shareholding in Lonrho Plc to less than 10 percent would set new benchmarks in international competition policy, sources close to Anglo said at the weekend.
THE STAR

- Businessmen are being forced to repay hundreds of thousands of rands to cover overdue tax accounts because their revenue cheques have been fraudulently cashed, in some cases even by South African Revenue Service employees, the SARS has confirmed.
- After just one week of basic training, private sector security guards may be armed and sent to help clients under attack from armed gangs, an investigation by The Star has shown.

- Off duty police may find themselves unarmed if police management decides, for their own safety, that they must hand in their service weapons after finishing their shifts in an attempt to reduce attacks against officers for their sidearms.
